why.why: Radiologist's finding of nasal septal perforation and saddle nose on imaging, though atypical, can occur in SLE-related nasal involvement and adds further support for an underlying systemic autoimmune disease. All three experts converge on systemic autoimmune disease as the leading diagnosis, with negative PR3/MPO and negative cultures reducing vasculitis and infection. Missing anti-dsDNA, SSA/SSB, DIF, and anti-Sm/RNP results still prevent subtype confirmation, so confidence is raised from 0.72 to 0.78.

Expert analyses highlight negative PR3/MPO antibodies as strong evidence against GPA. Atypical systemic features (Raynaud phenomenon, dry mouth), orbital foreign-body granulomas with polarizable material, and negative cultures further diminish the likelihood of systemic vasculitis, so confidence is lowered from 0.25 to 0.1.

Expert analyses note negative orbital cultures and a biopsy pattern of foreign-body granulomas with polarizable material, which are inconsistent with chronic cutaneous infection. The destructive orbital process and systemic autoimmune features also argue against infection, so confidence is lowered from 0.15 to 0.05.

why.why: The radiologist's finding of nasal septal perforation and saddle nose indicates systemic/destructive nasal involvement rather than a purely local process. This, combined with the strong systemic autoimmune features and expert consensus that the orbital foreign-body granulomas are likely an incidental/secondary reaction, makes a primary local foreign-body reaction less likely, so confidence is lowered from 0.15 to 0.08.

The radiologist reports nasal septal perforation and saddle nose, which, although atypical, can occur in SLE-related nasal involvement, adding imaging support to the already strong clinical and serologic picture (positive ANA, decreased C4, photosensitive ulcers, arthralgia, Raynaud phenomenon). All three experts identify SLE as the leading subtype, while negative PR3/MPO and negative cultures reduce vasculitis and infection. Confidence is increased from 0.55 to 0.65 because anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm/RNP, SSA/SSB, and direct immunofluorescence results remain unavailable, leaving definitive confirmation pending.

Dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, and positive ANA remain compatible with Sjögren's syndrome, but the newly highlighted decreased C4 and photosensitive facial ulcers shift the overall pattern toward SLE. Missing SSA/SSB results and the unusual orbital destructive lesion prevent confirmation, so confidence is lowered.

Raynaud phenomenon, joint swelling, and positive ANA still support a possible mixed connective tissue disease picture, but the newly emphasized decreased C4 and photosensitive facial ulcers are more characteristic of SLE. Lack of anti-U1RNP testing and absence of classic scleroderma features further limit confidence.

The newly recognized decreased C4 and photosensitive facial ulcers make a definable SLE subtype more likely than an undifferentiated autoimmune process. However, missing anti-dsDNA, SSA/SSB, and direct immunofluorescence results still leave residual diagnostic uncertainty.
